## Three estimates per activity {#pert}

```{=html}
<div class="formula"><p><i>t</i><sub>e</sub> = (<i>a</i> + 4<i>m</i> + <i>b</i>) / 6 &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; σ² = ((<i>b</i> − <i>a</i>) / 6)²</p></div>
<table class="wide">
  <thead><tr><th>Activity</th><th class="num">Optimistic a</th><th class="num">Most likely m</th><th class="num">Pessimistic b</th><th class="num">t<sub>e</sub></th><th class="num">σ²</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>A · Survey, permits</td><td class="num">2</td><td class="num">3</td><td class="num">6</td><td class="num">3.33</td><td class="num">0.44</td></tr>
    <tr><td>B · Design</td><td class="num">3</td><td class="num">4</td><td class="num">8</td><td class="num">4.50</td><td class="num">0.69</td></tr>
    <tr><td>C · Containers</td><td class="num">6</td><td class="num">8</td><td class="num">14</td><td class="num">8.67</td><td class="num hit">1.78</td></tr>
    <tr><td>D · Civil works</td><td class="num">3</td><td class="num">5</td><td class="num">7</td><td class="num">5.00</td><td class="num">0.44</td></tr>
    <tr><td>E · PCS, transformer</td><td class="num">5</td><td class="num">7</td><td class="num">9</td><td class="num">7.00</td><td class="num">0.44</td></tr>
    <tr><td>F · Install containers</td><td class="num">1</td><td class="num">2</td><td class="num">3</td><td class="num">2.00</td><td class="num">0.11</td></tr>
    <tr><td>G · Install PCS, grid</td><td class="num">2</td><td class="num">3</td><td class="num">5</td><td class="num">3.17</td><td class="num">0.25</td></tr>
    <tr><td>H · Commission</td><td class="num">1</td><td class="num">2</td><td class="num">4</td><td class="num">2.17</td><td class="num">0.25</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```

[Most estimates are skewed to the right: things go wrong more often than they go unusually well, so t~e~ is above m.]{.note-line}

## The PERT answer {#pert-answer}

::: {.two}
::: {}
With expected durations, the critical path is **A-B-C-F-H, 20.67 weeks**. A-B-E-G-H follows at 20.17 weeks.

PERT adds the variances along the critical path: σ² = 0.44 + 0.69 + 1.78 + 0.11 + 0.25 = 3.28, so σ = **1.81 weeks**.

P(finish ≤ 22) = Φ((22 − 20.67)/1.81) = Φ(0.74) = **0.77**.
:::
::: {}
::: {.route-question}
PERT looks only at one path. But the second path is just 0.5 week shorter. In the futures where E or G runs late, it decides the finish date, and PERT ignores those futures.
:::
:::
:::

## Check PERT by simulation {#pert-explorer data-hold="true"}

```{=html}
<div class="widget" id="px">
  <div class="w-controls"><label class="w-slider">Deadline, weeks <strong id="px-dv">22.0</strong><input type="range" id="px-d" min="18" max="26" step="0.25" value="22"></label></div>
  <svg id="px-svg" viewBox="0 0 1160 260" role="img" aria-label="Probability of finishing by each deadline, PERT against simulation"></svg>
  <div class="w-readout" id="px-out" aria-live="polite"></div>
</div>
<script>
(function () {
  const root = document.getElementById('px'); if (!root) return;
  root.addEventListener('click', (e) => e.stopPropagation());
  // Simulated P(finish <= deadline), 200,000 runs with beta-PERT durations, deadlines 18 to 26 by 0.25.
  const MC = [0.0236,0.0356,0.0526,0.0741,0.1006,0.1324,0.1706,0.2151,0.264,0.3161,0.3727,0.4298,0.4884,0.5471,0.6037,0.6566,0.7055,0.75,0.7908,0.8274,0.8596,0.8869,0.9095,0.9284,0.9443,0.957,0.9672,0.9757,0.9818,0.9865,0.99,0.9928,0.995];
  const T = 20.6667, SD = 1.8105;
  function erf(x) { const s = Math.sign(x); x = Math.abs(x); const t = 1 / (1 + 0.3275911 * x); return s * (1 - (((((1.061405429 * t - 1.453152027) * t) + 1.421413741) * t - 0.284496736) * t + 0.254829592) * t * Math.exp(-x * x)); }
  const pert = (d) => 0.5 * (1 + erf((d - T) / SD / Math.SQRT2));
  const W = 1160, H = 260, L = 70, R = 20, T0 = 10, B = 40, X = (d) => L + (d - 18) / 8 * (W - L - R), Y = (p) => T0 + (1 - p) * (H - T0 - B);
  function draw() {
    const d = +document.getElementById('px-d').value; document.getElementById('px-dv').textContent = d.toFixed(2);
    let g = '';
    for (const p of [0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1]) g += `<line x1="${L}" x2="${W - R}" y1="${Y(p)}" y2="${Y(p)}" stroke="#B9C1C6"/><text x="${L - 10}" y="${Y(p) + 6}" text-anchor="end" font-size="16" fill="#333F4A">${p}</text>`;
    for (let w = 18; w <= 26; w += 1) g += `<text x="${X(w)}" y="${H - 14}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="16" fill="#333F4A">${w}</text>`;
    let pp = '', mm = '';
    for (let i = 0; i <= 160; i++) { const x = 18 + i * 0.05; pp += (i ? 'L' : 'M') + X(x).toFixed(1) + ',' + Y(pert(x)).toFixed(1); }
    MC.forEach((p, i) => { mm += (i ? 'L' : 'M') + X(18 + i * 0.25).toFixed(1) + ',' + Y(p).toFixed(1); });
    g += `<path d="${pp}" fill="none" stroke="#0F6E6B" stroke-width="3" stroke-dasharray="8 6"/><path d="${mm}" fill="none" stroke="#E29A2D" stroke-width="3.5"/>`;
    const i = Math.round((d - 18) / 0.25), pm = MC[i], pe = pert(d);
    g += `<line x1="${X(d)}" x2="${X(d)}" y1="${T0}" y2="${H - B}" stroke="#1C242B" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="${X(d)}" cy="${Y(pe)}" r="6" fill="#0F6E6B"/><circle cx="${X(d)}" cy="${Y(pm)}" r="6" fill="#E29A2D"/>`;
    g += `<text x="${X(24.2)}" y="${Y(0.62)}" font-size="17" fill="#0F6E6B" font-weight="700">PERT, one path</text><text x="${X(24.2)}" y="${Y(0.5)}" font-size="17" fill="#9a5f10" font-weight="700">Simulation, all paths</text>`;
    document.getElementById('px-svg').innerHTML = g;
    document.getElementById('px-out').innerHTML = `Deadline ${d.toFixed(2)} weeks: PERT gives <b>${(pe * 100).toFixed(0)}%</b>, simulation gives <span class="best">${(pm * 100).toFixed(0)}%</span>. Gap: ${((pe - pm) * 100).toFixed(0)} points.`;
  }
  document.getElementById('px-d').addEventListener('input', draw);
  draw();
})();
</script>
```

[The simulation draws every duration from a beta-PERT distribution with the same a, m and b, and takes the longest path in each run.]{.hint}

## Merge bias {#merge-bias}

```{=html}
<table class="wide">
  <thead><tr><th>Deadline, weeks</th><th class="num">20</th><th class="num">21</th><th class="num">22</th><th class="num">23</th><th class="num">24</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>PERT, critical path only</td><td class="num">36%</td><td class="num">57%</td><td class="num">77%</td><td class="num">90%</td><td class="num">97%</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Simulation, all paths</td><td class="num">26%</td><td class="num">49%</td><td class="num hit">71%</td><td class="num">86%</td><td class="num">94%</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```

::: {.bridge}
The simulated mean finish is **21.1 weeks**, not 20.7. A-B-E-G-H turns out to be the longest path in **41%** of runs. Where paths merge, the finish date is the maximum of several uncertain paths, and that maximum is later than any one path alone.
:::

[For a 90% on-time promise, PERT suggests 23.0 weeks; the simulation says 23.4.]{.note-line}

## Crashing: buying time {#crashing}

```{=html}
<table class="wide">
  <thead><tr><th>Activity</th><th class="num">A</th><th class="num">B</th><th class="num">C</th><th class="num">D</th><th class="num">E</th><th class="num">F</th><th class="num">G</th><th class="num">H</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>Cost per week saved, CNY million</td><td class="num">0.40</td><td class="num">0.25</td><td class="num">0.30</td><td class="num">0.20</td><td class="num">0.35</td><td class="num">0.50</td><td class="num">0.45</td><td class="num">0.60</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Maximum weeks saved</td><td class="num">1</td><td class="num">1.5</td><td class="num">3</td><td class="num">2</td><td class="num">2</td><td class="num">0.5</td><td class="num">1</td><td class="num">0.5</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```

::: {.two}
::: {}
**Rules of thumb.** Crash only critical activities. Prefer the cheapest per week. An activity shared by both long paths (A, B or H) shortens both at once.
:::
::: {}
**As an LP.** Choose crash weeks x~k~ to minimize Σ c~k~ x~k~, with every path's expected length minus its crashing at most 19, and 0 ≤ x~k~ ≤ max~k~. Block 2 solves LPs like this in Solver.
:::
:::

## Plan your crash {#crash-explorer data-hold="true"}

```{=html}
<div class="widget" id="kx">
  <div class="ahp-grid" id="kx-s"></div>
  <table class="wide" id="kx-t"></table>
  <div class="w-readout" id="kx-out" aria-live="polite"></div>
</div>
<script>
(function () {
  const root = document.getElementById('kx'); if (!root) return;
  root.addEventListener('click', (e) => e.stopPropagation());
  const te = { A: 20 / 6, B: 4.5, C: 52 / 6, D: 5, E: 7, F: 2, G: 19 / 6, H: 13 / 6 };
  const cost = { A: 0.40, B: 0.25, C: 0.30, D: 0.20, E: 0.35, F: 0.50, G: 0.45, H: 0.60 }, mx = { A: 1, B: 1.5, C: 3, D: 2, E: 2, F: 0.5, G: 1, H: 0.5 };
  const paths = [['A', 'B', 'C', 'F', 'H'], ['A', 'B', 'E', 'G', 'H'], ['A', 'D', 'G', 'H'], ['A', 'D', 'F', 'H']];
  document.getElementById('kx-s').innerHTML = Object.keys(te).map((k) => `<label class="ahp-pair"><span class="ahp-l">${k} (${cost[k].toFixed(2)})</span><input type="range" min="0" max="${mx[k]}" step="${1 / 6}" value="0" data-k="${k}"><span class="ahp-r">max ${mx[k]}</span><b data-v="${k}">0</b></label>`).join('');
  function draw() {
    const x = {}; root.querySelectorAll('input[data-k]').forEach((el) => { x[el.dataset.k] = +el.value; root.querySelector(`b[data-v="${el.dataset.k}"]`).textContent = (+el.value).toFixed(2); });
    const len = paths.map((p) => p.reduce((s, k) => s + te[k] - x[k], 0)), T = Math.max(...len);
    const c = Object.keys(x).reduce((s, k) => s + x[k] * cost[k], 0);
    document.getElementById('kx-t').innerHTML = '<thead><tr><th>Path</th>' + paths.map((p) => `<th class="num">${p.join('-')}</th>`).join('') + '</tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Expected length, weeks</td>' +
      len.map((l) => `<td class="num${Math.abs(l - T) < 1e-6 ? ' hit' : ''}">${l.toFixed(2)}</td>`).join('') + '</tr></tbody>';
    document.getElementById('kx-out').innerHTML = `Project: <b>${T.toFixed(2)} weeks</b>, crash cost <b>CNY ${c.toFixed(3)} million</b>. ` +
      (T <= 19.001 ? `<span class="best">19-week target met</span>` : `Still ${(T - 19).toFixed(2)} weeks over the 19-week target.`);
  }
  root.addEventListener('input', draw);
  draw();
})();
</script>
```

[Sliders move in steps of one sixth of a week. The number in brackets is the cost per week, in CNY million.]{.hint}

## Activity · Crash auction {#act1 .activity data-hold="true"}

[Groups of 4 · 30 minutes · price list and the planner]{.act-label}

::: {.prompt}
Reach 19 expected weeks at the lowest crash cost. The cheapest valid plan wins.
:::

1. Plan on paper first, using the rules of thumb. Write your plan and its cost.
2. Check it on the planner. Did any crash week buy nothing? Why?
3. If every week saved also saves CNY 0.30 million of site overhead, how far should CellCo crash?
4. Each group posts its plan and cost. Then we reveal the LP optimum.

::: {.selfstudy}
Studying alone: find a plan that meets 19 weeks for under CNY 0.5 million before you go on.
:::

## Activity · Answer {#act1-answer}

::: {.two}
::: {}
```{=html}
<table class="wide">
  <thead><tr><th>Target, weeks</th><th>LP optimal crashing</th><th class="num">Cost, CNY million</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>20</td><td>B 0.67</td><td class="num">0.167</td></tr>
    <tr><td>19</td><td>B 1.5, C 0.17</td><td class="num hit">0.425</td></tr>
    <tr><td>18.5</td><td>A 0.17, B 1.5, C 0.5</td><td class="num">0.592</td></tr>
    <tr><td>18</td><td>A 0.67, B 1.5, C 0.5</td><td class="num">0.792</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```
:::
::: {}
B is shared by both long paths and is the cheapest critical activity, so it goes first. Crashing D buys nothing: D is not critical.

With overhead of CNY 0.30 million per week, crashing pays while the marginal cost is below 0.30: B (0.25) pays, C (0.30) breaks even, A (0.40) does not. So crash B fully.
:::
:::

[These are expected durations. Crashing to 19 expected weeks still leaves a real chance of finishing later.]{.note-line}

## What we learned {#debrief}

::: {.takeaways}
::: {.tk}
PERT turns three estimates into an expected duration and a variance. For CellCo it gives a 77% chance of finishing in 22 weeks.
:::
::: {.tk}
Simulation of all paths gives 71% and a mean of 21.1 weeks. Merging paths make PERT optimistic.
:::
::: {.tk .key}
Crashing is an LP. Finishing in 19 expected weeks costs at least CNY 0.425 million, by crashing B, which both long paths share, and a little of C.
:::
:::

[Session 9: what happens when two activities need the same installation crew.]{.note-line}
